context_line: Informal hello to one person you call tu: a friend, a child, family. Not for an elder, a boss or a stranger; to them say Laba diena. It is also the first word of labas rytas / laba diena / labas vakaras.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1, §2.5: 'Vyresniam už save asmeniui, viršininkui, profesoriui nederėtų sakyti net vieną sveikinimosi žodį labas ar sveikas'; also lt.wiktionary 'labas': 'sakoma sveikinantis (neformaliai)'

context_line: Plural of sveikas: hello to several people, or to one person you call jūs. Neutral and common in shops and offices, but still a one-word greeting: with an elder or a superior Laba diena is the safer choice.
source_note: en.wiktionary 'sveiki' (to more than one person) and 'sveikas' (informal, to a male); Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1 (Sveikas, drauguži! Sveiki, vaikai!) and §2.5 (labas/sveikas not to superiors). The jūs-singular use of Sveiki is everyday practice but not stated in a source I could read — hence medium.

context_line: On first meeting in the morning; to anyone, tu or jūs. At home the one who gets up later greets those already up. Labą rytą (accusative) is equally correct.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1 (both cases correct, nominative preferred), §2.5 (family custom)

context_line: The all-purpose polite daytime greeting for shops, offices, strangers and anyone you call jūs. Use it where labas would be too familiar. Labą dieną is equally correct.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1, §2.5. VLKK consultation 8094 'laba diena / gera diena' exists (https://www.vlkk.lt/konsultacijos/8094-laba-diena-gera-diena-labintis-pasilabinti) but vlkk.lt could not be fetched from this session (Cloudflare challenge); title only.

context_line: Said on meeting in the evening (arriving at a door, entering a shop late in the day). When parting for the night the word is labanakt, not labas vakaras.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1 lists labas vakaras among greetings; §3 places labanakt(is) at parting 'vakare, prieš naktį'

context_line: Only when parting for the night or going to bed, never on arrival. Short for labanaktis; fits everyone and every occasion. The diminutive labos naktelės is familiar.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3: 'labanaktis ar trumpesnė jo forma labanakt tinka visiems ir visais atvejais'; also en.wiktionary 'labanaktis'

context_line: The neutral everyday farewell, accepted standard, fits anyone. Viso labo is the more Lithuanian variant; the clipped viso! is teenage talk; viso geriausio is familiar and not for people you respect.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3

context_line: The old word (from su Dievu, 'with God'). The etiquette guide calls it the best and most Lithuanian farewell; it faded under Soviet anti-religious pressure, and many speakers now keep it for long or final partings.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3 ('Geriausia, lietuviškiausia atsisveikinti… sudiev! arba sudie!'); Jasiūnaitė 1997 §29 on its decline under atheist propaganda (https://journals.vu.lt/kalbotyra/article/download/31319/30283/73015); 'final partings' rests on en.wiktionary 'sudie' glossing 'adieu' — medium.

context_line: Literally 'till we meet'. Accepted standard, but the etiquette guide classes it with iki vakaro / iki rytojaus as a farewell for people you are close to; broadcasters also use it to an audience.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3: 'Tokius atsisveikinimus galime tarti tik artimiems žmonėms… Atsisveikinam iki kito karto!'

context_line: The one-word farewell between friends, favoured by teenagers and young people. Fine in its place; not for a stranger, an elder or a superior.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3: 'Su draugais kartais lakoniškai atsisveikiname tik vienu žodžiu iki… paauglių, jaunuolių mėgstami'; en.wiktionary 'iki' (interjection: bye)

context_line: Iki + genitive, like iki vakaro, iki susitikimo. Same register as iki pasimatymo — people you know; to a stranger say viso gero.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §3

context_line: Ačiū and dėkui are exact synonyms in every register. The replies: prašom (warm) or nėra už ką (modest). An answer to 'how are you?' begins with it: Ačiū, gerai.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2 ('absoliučiais sinonimais'), §6.3 (replies), §6.2 end (Ačiū, gerai!)

context_line: But not more casual than ačiū: the two are exact synonyms, both standard and both spoken. Dėkui is the one with a family: dėkoti, padėka, dėkingas.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2. Note for the owner: the deck's gloss 'thanks' hints at a register difference the reference denies.

context_line: Labai ačiū / labai dėkui is the correct intensifier (didelis ačiū is a Russian calque to avoid); labai labai ačiū for real gratitude. Dėkoju or esu labai dėkingas are politer still.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2

context_line: 1st person singular of prašyti. The cooler, more official of the pair — at home in requests and orders (Prašau pranešti…). As a reply to thanks or when handing something over, prašom is warmer and more usual. Put it before the verb, never after (not 'Pasakykit, prašau').
source_note: en.wiktionary 'prašom' usage notes (citing VLKK 9416 'prašom, prašau, prašyčiau…', https://www.vlkk.lt/konsultacijos/9416-prasom-prasau-prasyciau-prasome-prasytume — not fetched, Cloudflare); Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.1–7.3

context_line: Also: please / you're welcome. The warm, hospitable form — inviting someone in, offering food, handing something over, and the usual reply to ačiū. Grammatically plural but said by one speaker; more common than prašau in speech.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.3, §7.1; en.wiktionary 'prašom' (Balčikonis recommended prašom over prašau)

context_line: Also: not at all (lit. 'there is nothing for'). The modest folk reply to thanks, playing the favour down. Prašom is the other reply, fitting when the favour was real. Informal: nėr už ką.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.3 ('Yra dar liaudiškas atsakymas dėkojančiam: Nėr už ką!'); en.wiktionary 'nėra už ką'

context_line: Also: it's nothing. The reply to someone's atsiprašau after a bump or a small mishap — said quietly with a nod (Nieko! or Nieko tokio!). Never answer an apology with prašau. Not a reply to thanks.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.4: 'Palenkiant galvą, tinka… atsakyti: Nieko! (Nieko tokio!)'; prašau in that slot 'išeina nei šis, nei tas'

context_line: Literally 'nothing terrible': fills the same slot as nieko tokio, reassuring someone who apologises or worries.
source_note: No source read states this phrase; en.wiktionary has no entry (404). The etiquette guide gives only Nieko! / Nieko tokio! in the apology-reply slot. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Excuse me (to get attention or to get past): 1st person 'I apologise', so it fits tu and jūs alike. The standard opener to a stranger: Atsiprašau! Gal galėtumėt pasakyti…. When it means 'let me through', the reply is prašom.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.4, §8.1–8.2; en.wiktionary 'atsiprašau' ('request for attention, to pass or for an apology')

context_line: The same word as the excuse-me, now an apology after the fact (a bump, a broken cup). The other person answers Nieko (tokio), not prašau. To say what for: Atsiprašau už….
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.4; lt.wiktionary 'atsiprašyti' example 'Atsiprašau už įžeidimą'

context_line: Also: forgive me, formal. Imperative of atleisti 'to forgive' in the jūs form (to a tu-person: Atleisk). It asks pardon rather than announcing an apology, so it sounds a shade weightier than atsiprašau; also when you have forgotten something: Atleiskit, išdilo iš atminties.
source_note: en.wiktionary 'atleisti' (to forgive, pardon); Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §10.1 example; Wikivoyage phrasebook (https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lithuanian_phrasebook) gives Atleiskite for 'excuse me (begging pardon)' and 'I'm sorry'

context_line: Indicative galite (jūs): direct, fine with service staff. The conditional galėtumėte (next card) is the gentler form the etiquette guide recommends to strangers and elders, usually with gal: Gal galėtumėt….
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §8.1

context_line: Could you help me? Conditional mood, the politest request. 'Gal galėtumėt…' is singled out as very polite and very gentle — for a stranger, an elder or anyone you respect.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §8.1: 'dalelytė gal kartu su tariamosios nuosakos veiksmažodžiu galėtumėt labai mandagiai, labai švelniai išreiškia kreipimąsi į nepažįstamą vyresnį ar šiaip gerbtiną žmogų'

context_line: The jūs form: respect, formality, distance. To a child or a friend: Kiek tau metų? (sentence card S-0051). Young Lithuanians themselves often hesitate between tu and jūs.
source_note: Ivanauskaitė & Hilbig 2023, Taikomoji kalbotyra 19: plural address = respect, formality, polite distance; singular = friendliness, intimacy, familiarity

context_line: How old are you?, the tu form: for a child, a friend, family. Tu signals friendliness and closeness; to an adult you don't know, use jūs: Kiek jums metų?
source_note: Ivanauskaitė & Hilbig 2023 (as above). Sentence note type — field to be decided by the executor.

context_line: Literally 'how is it going'. Asked of people you know. The answer begins with thanks: Ačiū, gerai.
variant_tu_jus: with a person: Kaip tau sekasi? (tu) / Kaip jums sekasi? (jūs)
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2 end: 'Atsakymą visuomet turime pradėti padėkos žodžiu: Ačiū (dėkui), gerai!' The tu/jūs register of Kaip sekasi itself is not stated in a source read.

context_line: In full, Ačiū, gerai: Lithuanian etiquette starts the answer to 'how are you?' with a word of thanks.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2 end

context_line: Literally 'pleasant to get acquainted'. Said on being introduced. The younger or less senior person introduces themselves first, a man before a woman; in a formal meeting give your surname, not only your first name.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §10.1; en.wiktionary 'malonu' (Malonu susipažinti su jumis)

context_line: Literally 'healthy, having arrived'. The set phrase for guests who have travelled to you. Plural form, used to one person or many. For someone already at the door, Prašom! or Užeikite! invites them in.
variant_tu_jus: to one tu-person: Sveikas atvykęs (m.) / Sveika atvykusi (f.)
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.1: 'Iš toliau atkeliavę svečiai sveikinami žodžių junginiu sveiki atvykę!'; §7.3 on prašom at the door

context_line: Jūs imperative (Užeik! to a tu-person). The etiquette guide prefers a plain Prašom! at the door and marks 'Įeikit(e), prašau!' as rude.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.3 discusses įeikite, not užeikite; the transfer to užeikite is mine.

context_line: On the telephone only, when answering a private line (Klausau, 'I'm listening', is the other). At a workplace answer with the office or your name, not alio.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §11: 'Ar visada tinka telefonu atsakyti žodžiu klausau arba alio? Ne, ne visada!'

context_line: Jūs form (kalbate), the right one for a stranger. The verb ending carries the register; the pronoun can be dropped.
source_note: Ivanauskaitė & Hilbig 2023 (register); kalbėti: kalbi / kalbate — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Jūsų (your, jūs) to an adult you don't know; tavo to a child or a peer you already call tu.
source_note: Ivanauskaitė & Hilbig 2023 (register); possessive pronouns jūsų/tavo

context_line: Jūs to a stranger or an elder; tu between young people and friends.
source_note: Ivanauskaitė & Hilbig 2023

context_line: Jūs form (gyvenate). To a friend: Kur gyveni?
source_note: gyventi: gyveni / gyvenate — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Jūs form (dirbate); kuo is the instrumental: 'as what do you work?' To a friend: Kuo dirbi?
source_note: dirbti: dirbi / dirbate — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Galite is the indicative jūs form: plain and polite enough. The gentler version is the conditional: Ar galėtumėte pakartoti? / Gal galėtumėt pakartoti?
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §8.1 (gal + galėtumėt); galėti: gali / galite / galėtum / galėtumėte — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Jūs form, as to a waiter. Conditional galėtumėte is softer; the tu form gali is for a friend.
variant_tu_jus: tu: Ar gali ką nors rekomenduoti?
source_note: galėti forms — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary; rekomenduoti has no en.wiktionary entry

context_line: Prašom + infinitive, the order the 2004 etiquette reference recommends (§7.3); it marks the everyday Kalbėkite lėčiau, prašau as a Russian-pattern calque.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.2–7.3 marks prašau AFTER an imperative ('Pakartokite, prašau') as an 'atbulinis prašau', a Russian-pattern calque to avoid, and recommends prašom + infinitive (Prašom pakartoti). Modern speech uses the postposed form constantly and VLKK's current view could not be checked (site unreachable). Owner's call whether the card's Lithuanian stays; the note on the back can carry the recommended form. kalbėti: kalbėk / kalbėkite — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Prašom + infinitive, the polite Lithuanian request (the 2004 etiquette reference, §7.3). The everyday Pakartokite, prašau is marked there as a Russian-pattern calque. Same picture as Ar galite pakartoti?; the question is the softer of the two.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.2–7.3 marks prašau AFTER an imperative ('Pakartokite, prašau') as an 'atbulinis prašau', a Russian-pattern calque to avoid, and recommends prašom + infinitive (Prašom pakartoti). Modern speech uses the postposed form constantly and VLKK's current view could not be checked (site unreachable). Owner's call whether the card's Lithuanian stays; the note on the back can carry the recommended form. pakartoti: pakartok / pakartokite — regular morphology; conjugation table not fetched (Wiktionary rate limit) — form unverified

context_line: Prašom + infinitive (the 2004 etiquette reference, §7.3). The everyday Užrašykite, prašau is marked there as a Russian-pattern calque.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.2–7.3 marks prašau AFTER an imperative ('Pakartokite, prašau') as an 'atbulinis prašau', a Russian-pattern calque to avoid, and recommends prašom + infinitive (Prašom pakartoti). Modern speech uses the postposed form constantly and VLKK's current view could not be checked (site unreachable). Owner's call whether the card's Lithuanian stays; the note on the back can carry the recommended form. užrašyti: užrašyk / užrašykite — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Prašom + the infinitive of the reflexive sėstis (the 2004 etiquette reference, §7.3); with a gesture to the chair a plain Prašom is enough. The everyday Sėskitės, prašau is marked there as a calque.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.2–7.3 marks prašau AFTER an imperative ('Pakartokite, prašau') as an 'atbulinis prašau', a Russian-pattern calque to avoid, and recommends prašom + infinitive (Prašom pakartoti). Modern speech uses the postposed form constantly and VLKK's current view could not be checked (site unreachable). Owner's call whether the card's Lithuanian stays; the note on the back can carry the recommended form. sėstis: sėskis / sėskitės — regular morphology; conjugation table not fetched (Wiktionary rate limit) — form unverified

context_line: Noun + prašau is not the imperative pattern the reference condemns, but it still prefers the politeness word first: Prašom sąskaitą.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.3 ('lietuviai nuo seno yra įpratę pirmiausia tarti mandagumo žodį'); the extension to a noun object is mine

context_line: Iškvieskite is the jūs/plural imperative, right for shouting to bystanders; to one person you know: Iškviesk gydytoją!
source_note: iškviesti: iškviesk / iškvieskite — regular morphology; conjugation table not fetched (Wiktionary rate limit) — form unverified

context_line: Literally 'save me!' The clipped plural imperative of gelbėti, shouted to anyone within earshot; an emergency word, not a request (that is Ar galite man padėti? / Man reikia pagalbos).
source_note: en.wiktionary 'gelbėti' (to save, rescue); imperative gelbėk / gelbėkit(e) — regular morphology; conjugation table not fetched (Wiktionary rate limit) — form unverified

context_line: Pasveik is the tu imperative, so this is for family and friends; to someone you call jūs: Greitai pasveikite! Wishes are otherwise mostly genitives: sveikatos!
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.2 (wishes in the genitive or the imperative: 'neliūdėk, nebijok… būk laimingas'); pasveikti: pasveik / pasveikite — regular morphology; conjugation table not fetched (Wiktionary rate limit) — form unverified

context_line: Eikite is the jūs imperative, the form a stranger gives you; to a friend: Eik tiesiai.
source_note: eiti: eik / eikite — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Tu form (eini), so family and friends; to an adult you don't know: Kur jūs einate? (and a stranger would rarely ask).
source_note: eiti: eini / einate — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Tu form (veiki), the casual phone opener between friends; jūs: Ką veikiate?
source_note: veikti: veiki / veikiate — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Jūs form (turite), the shop question. To a friend: Ar turi…?
source_note: turėti: turi / turite — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: Noriu is the plain indicative: direct, fine at home or for a child. For a polite request use the conditional norėčiau (next cards).
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §7.4 (the conditional as the gentlest request form, shown with prašyčiau); norėti: noriu / norėčiau — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary. The transfer from prašyčiau to norėčiau is mine.

context_line: Norėčiau is the conditional of norėti: the polite way to order or ask. Noriu kavos is blunter (family, children). Kavos is genitive: 'some coffee'.
source_note: as A2-0916; norėti forms — conjugation table read on en.wiktionary

context_line: The conditional softens a wish into a request; the standard opener in a café, shop or hotel. Noriu… is what you say at home.
Norėčiau + infinitive, the polite request pattern; same register as Norėčiau kavos.
The neutral agreement word (lit. 'known'). Aišku is brisker ('clear!'), be abejo ('without doubt') more emphatic.
source_note: No source read compares žinoma / aišku / be abejo; the shading is my own and should be checked by the owner. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: As an answer, a brisk colloquial 'sure, obviously'; as an adverb, 'clearly'. Neutral cousin: žinoma.
source_note: as A2-0883. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Literally 'without doubt'; a shade more emphatic and formal than žinoma.
source_note: as A2-0883. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Accusative of akimirka 'an instant'; a shop assistant's or receptionist's word. Minutėlę! is the warmer diminutive twin; both fit tu and jūs.
source_note: Deck note on A2-1169 gives 'Minutėlę!'; no external source read. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Said as Minutėlę! (accusative), the diminutive making it friendly; akimirką is the plainer twin.
source_note: as A2-0884. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Neuter adjective used as an exclamation; neutral register. Šaunu is more colloquial, nuostabu/nuostabus stronger ('wonderful'), labai gerai the sober 'very good'.
source_note: No source read grades puiku / šaunu / nuostabu / labai gerai; owner to check. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Colloquial, youthful; puiku is the neutral equivalent. Šaunuolis (the person) is 'good lad / well done'.
source_note: as A2-1154. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: Stronger than puiku; as an exclamation the neuter nuostabu! The card's form is the masculine adjective.
source_note: as A2-1154. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: A pity / I'm sorry (sympathy or regret: Gaila!, Man gaila) — not an apology. For your own fault say atsiprašau.
source_note: Deck decision on A2-0881 (notes column: changed from 'Man gaila', which means 'I feel sorry'); no external source read.

context_line: Everything's fine / all good — the reassuring answer to a worried question; as a reply to Kaip sekasi? start with thanks: Ačiū, viskas gerai.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2 end (Ačiū, gerai)

context_line: The honest middling answer to Kaip sekasi?; between friends, not to a boss. The polite default is Ačiū, gerai.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §6.2 end gives the polite default; the register of šiaip sau is my reading

context_line: Literally 'how many hours?' The everyday way to ask; Kuri valanda? ('which hour?') is the other. Both are standard; Kuri (dabar) valanda? is the form the 2004 etiquette reference puts in its polite example.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §8.1 example 'Gal galėtumėt pasakyti, kuri dabar valanda?'; the status of Kiek valandų? is not stated in a source read

context_line: Literally 'which hour?' Shares its picture with Kiek valandų?; this is the form in the etiquette reference's polite example: Atsiprašau! Gal galėtumėt pasakyti, kuri dabar valanda?
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §8.1

context_line: The same question as Kiek kainuoja? with tai ('this/that') said out loud; one picture serves both.
source_note: Transparent syntax; no source needed beyond the words, but none read either. Owner: approved as written (2026-10-18).

context_line: A parting WISH in the genitive (geros dienos), like sėkmės, geros kelionės. Laba diena, in the nominative, is the greeting on meeting. Don't swap them.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.1–4.2: wishes 'dažniausiai reiškiami kilmininko linksniu'; 'labos nakties' as the genitive wish

context_line: Genitive of sėkmė 'success', the wish pattern (laimės, sveikatos, sėkmės). Said before an exam, an interview, a game; to anyone. The reply starts with ačiū.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.2 ('laimės, sėkmės, pasisekimo, sveikatos')

context_line: Have a good trip — genitive wish, for someone leaving on a journey; Sėkmės! is for an undertaking. Reply: Ačiū.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.2 (genitive wishes; thanks as the reply)

context_line: Genitive wish; between colleagues on a Friday, any register.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.2

context_line: Genitive wish ('of the tasty'); said to people about to eat or already eating, also by someone leaving the table first. The reference prefers Gero apetito! / Skanių pietų! and finds Skanaus apetito! illogical.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.1: 'Einančiam pietauti… Gerų pietų! Skanių pietų! Gero apetito!… Neretai girdime sakant: Skanaus apetito! arba tiesiog Skanaus!'

context_line: Literally 'to health'. The toast; also the host's folk reply to thanks for food or a bath (Ačiū už šilumą! — Į sveikatą!). The reference says NOT to say it to someone who sneezes except jokingly within the family.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §4.1 ('Čiaudinčiam žmogui linkėti į sveikatą netinka') and §6.3 (reply to thanks). Note: the deck's confusable 'Bless you (same words)' should be reconsidered.

context_line: The su + instrumental greeting pattern, widespread in speech and tolerated in the standard, though Jablonskis disliked it. On a card you can also write Sveikinu gimtadienio proga.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.2

context_line: 'I congratulate (you)'; sveikinu / sveikiname is the form for cards, letters and formal occasions, often with nuoširdžiai. In speech the su-pattern is commoner: Su jubiliejumi!
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.2

context_line: The genitive wish, the more Lithuanian pattern; the spoken Su Naujaisiais metais! is the su-pattern the standard tolerates.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.2 (Jablonskis: 'Sveikinu Naujųjų metų!'; su-pattern in speech)

context_line: Genitive wish ('of merry Christmas'); Su šventėmis! is the all-purpose su-pattern cousin for any holiday.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.2, §4.2

context_line: Su + instrumental, generic for any festive season; the standard tolerates the su-pattern in speech, the genitive wish (Linksmų Kalėdų!) is the more Lithuanian form.
source_note: Kniūkšta (ed.), Kompiuterinis lietuvių kalbos žinynas, ch. 'Kalbos etiketas' (Šviesa 2004) §2.2
